headings.text: A. Add a NEW product integration
A2. docker-compose.yml — register the service for real deployments
A3. docker-compose-local.yml — local registry / image overrides
B. Update an EXISTING submodule (pointer bump)

blocks.html:
This is the canonical workflow for getting a product integration API into the legacy docker-rasenmaeher-integration stack. Components there are git submodules, so "registering" your integration means two layers of pull request: one in your repo, and one in the integration-compose repo that wires the service into compose, miniwerk, and nginx. If you have not run the stack yet, do Set up your dev environment (Docker Compose) first.

Reminder on terms: the integration-compose's api/ submodule is the core rmapi (pvarki/python-rasenmaeher-api). Your service is a product integration API (like pvarki/python-matrix-rmapi), not "rmapi".

Two paths

blocks.code:
flowchart TB
    Q{"Is your product already\na submodule in the stack?"}
    Q -->|No| NEW["Add it: new submodule + compose/miniwerk/nginx edits"]
    Q -->|"Yes (e.g. api, takintegration)"| UPD["Update it: PR in submodule repo, then bump the pointer"]

blocks.html:
A. Add a NEW product integration

Open one PR against docker-rasenmaeher-integration that adds your repo as a submodule and makes the compose-level edits. Per the README, submodules "are repos in their own right" — yours will be no different.

A1. Add the submodule

From the repo root, add your integration's repo into its own directory (matching the existing pattern: api, takintegration, battlelog, matrixrmapi, …):

git submodule add https://github.com/<org>/<your-integration> <dir>
git add .gitmodules <dir>

Tell collaborators to run git submodule update --init --recursive after they pull your branch.

A2. docker-compose.yml — register the service for real deployments

Add a service block modelled on matrixrmapi (the reference) or takrmapi. The load-bearing parts:

  • Image + build: image: ${PVARKI_DOCKER_REPO:-ghcr.io/}pvarki/<your-image>:<tag> with build.context: ./<dir>, target: production.
  • Networks: join productnet (so nginx can reach you) and intranet. Do not publish your internal port here — traffic comes through nginx on 4626.
  • **depends_on**: rmnginx healthy (plus any backing service your product needs).
  • Volumes: at minimum ca_public:/ca_public (CA chain to validate the core's mTLS cert), your product's kraftwerk_shared_<product>:/pvarki (where miniwerk writes the manifest), a persistent data volume, and ui_files:/ui_files if you ship Deploy App UI assets.
  • **healthcheck**: e.g. test: '<yourcli> healthcheck || exit 1'.
  • Route it on 4626: add your upstream to the shared productsnginx service via env vars, mirroring NGINX_MATRIX_UPSTREAM / NGINX_MATRIX_UPSTREAM_PORT (which point at matrixrmapi:8012). productsnginx is what publishes 4626 (PRODUCT_HTTPS_PORT) and proxies mtls.<product>.<domain> to your service. Add your service to its depends_on too.
  • Register the product with miniwerk so it issues your subdomain + cert and writes your manifest: add your short-name to the miniwerk service's MW_PRODUCTS (today "tak,kc,bl,mtx,matrix,synapse"), add MW_<PRODUCT>__API_PORT: *productport (i.e. 4626) and MW_<PRODUCT>__USER_PORT, and mount a kraftwerk_shared_<product> volume into miniwerk at /pvarkishares/<product>.

The nginx hostname map and miniwerk's product defaults are not pure env-config. nginx/templates_consolidated/default.conf.template enumerates product hostnames (matrix.${NGINX_HOST}, mtls.matrix.${NGINX_HOST}, …), and miniwerk's src/miniwerk/config.py defines the canonical ProductSettings (subdomain + api_port/user_port, defaulting to 4626). A genuinely new product needs both touched: add your <product>.${NGINX_HOST} + mtls.<product>.${NGINX_HOST} rows to the nginx map blocks, and add your ProductSettings entry to the miniwerk config (then update tests/test_config.py, which asserts the exact FQDN set). These changes may live in the nginx/ tree and the miniwerk submodule respectively. TODO: confirm with maintainers whether the nginx template change ships in docker-rasenmaeher-integration directly or via the miniwerk/nginx submodule for your specific product.

A3. docker-compose-local.yml — local registry / image overrides

For the rmlocal composition, add the same service with the -local image suffix (e.g. pvarki/<your-image>:<tag>-local) so it builds and pushes to the local registry on localhost:5050. The Matrix example also publishes its internal port for debugging — keep the comment that warns never to expose it in production:

ports:
  - "8012:8012"  # NOTE: Do *NOT* expose this in production, always pass through NGinx proxy

A4. docker-compose-dev.yml — dev-mode (uvicorn --reload) overrides

For the rmdev composition, add an override that runs your service in reload mode with source bind-mounted, modelled on takrmapi:

  • build.target set to your image's devel/shell stage,
  • volumes mounting your source into the container (e.g. ./<dir>:/app, plus ./<dir>/ui:/ui if you have a UI),
  • a command/entrypoint that runs uvicorn --host 0.0.0.0 --port <internal> --reload --factory <module>:get_app (the Matrix docker/entrypoint-dev.sh does exactly this on 8012),
  • add your service to productsnginx.depends_on here too (the dev file re-declares it so it doesn't start too early).

A5. The localhost-resolution note (unofficial integrations)

Local testing reaches you at mtls.<product>.localmaeher.dev.pvarki.fi:4626. Official (OpenDefence-developed) integrations have their localmaeher subdomain resolved to localhost automatically by pvarki DNS. If your integration is NOT official, you must make its subdomain resolve to localhost yourself, e.g.:

rmlocal build <yourservice> --pull --push
rmlocal up
curl -k https://mtls.<product>.localmaeher.dev.pvarki.fi:4626/api/v1/healthcheck

When it comes up clean in rmlocal (and ideally rmdev), open the PR against docker-rasenmaeher-integration containing the submodule addition plus the four-file edits above.

B. Update an EXISTING submodule (pointer bump)

To ship a change to a submodule already in the stack — your own integration, the core api (rmapi), takintegration, etc. — the integration-compose repo only stores a pointer to a commit, so it is a two-PR dance:

  1. In the submodule's own repo: branch, commit, push, open a PR there, and get it merged (submodules are full repos — "create new branch, commit and push changes as usual under that directory").
  2. In **docker-rasenmaeher-integration**: bump the submodule pointer to the merged commit/tag:

git -C <dir> fetch
git -C <dir> checkout <merged-commit-or-tag>
git add <dir>
git commit -m "Bump <dir> to <tag>"

Then open a PR with that pointer bump. The integration-compose pins submodule combinations with tags, so prefer checking out a released tag of the submodule over a loose commit where one exists. Collaborators pick up the new pointer with git submodule update --init --recursive.
